why: Phase-2 singles on MOSEv2+VOST dev (OR0, OR7, OR7W, OR8, OR4 complete): OR8 (GT-re-encoded memory) +0.149 / +0.330 is by far the largest; OR7 (GT admission) +0.054 / +0.049; OR4 (GT geometry) +0.021 / +0.062. Under OR8 drift episodes still START about as often as OR0 (92 vs 106, 124 vs 140) but last 1.6 frames instead of 4.2 / 9.7. Combinations are chosen to answer: what remains when memory is perfect (geometry? selection?), and whether geometry adds to admission.

definitions.C48: OR4 + OR8: perfect geometry AND perfect memory -> residual = per-frame decoding/capacity
definitions.C58: OR5S + OR8: GT-best of the 7-member pool as output, with perfect memory -> are remaining drift onsets selectable?
definitions.C47: OR4 + OR7: perfect geometry AND GT memory admission (interaction of geometry with admission)
definitions.C75: OR5S + OR7: candidate selection AND GT memory admission (no GT mask anywhere)
definitions.OR8K10: OR8 but the GT re-encoding happens only on frames t % 10 == 0 (sparse perfect refresh; other frames native)

metrics: same as preregistration.json; interaction = dAB - (dA + dB) per dataset, video-equal, bootstrap over videos
order: appended after the 13 singles in queue order; dev split; same pod
